questions.question: In classical dance, which of the following Rasa represents "anger"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raudra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In classical Indian dance, "Raudra" represents the emotion of **anger**.
 
• Raudra is one of the **Navarasas** or nine essential emotions in Indian classical arts.
 
• Raudra Rasa is often depicted with **furrowed brows, wide eyes, and intense expressions** to convey anger or fury.
 
• This Rasa is used to portray characters who are **enraged or engaged in battle**, showcasing the intensity of the emotion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Navarasas:**

 
 
• The term "Navarasas" refers to the nine fundamental emotions or sentiments in Indian classical arts, including dance, music, and drama.
 
• The Navarasas are: Shringara (Love), Hasya (Humor), Karuna (Compassion), Raudra (Anger), Veera (Courage), Bhayanaka (Fear), Bibhatsa (Disgust), Adbhuta (Wonder), and Shanta (Peace).
 
 
 
• **Importance in Dance:**
 
 
• Each Rasa in classical dance allows the performer to express a wide range of human emotions, making the performance more engaging and relatable to the audience.
 
• Mastering the Navarasas is essential for dancers as it enhances their ability to convey stories and emotions effectively through their performance.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The concept of Rasa is rooted in ancient Indian texts like the **Natyashastra**, a comprehensive treatise on performing arts written by Bharata Muni.
 
• The Natyashastra outlines the theory of Rasa, explaining how different emotions are evoked and experienced by the audience.
 
 
 
• **Practical Application:**
 
 
• In practical terms, dancers use various facial expressions, hand gestures (mudras), and body movements to depict each Rasa.
 
• For Raudra, specific techniques like furrowing the brows, flaring the nostrils, and forceful movements are employed to effectively convey the emotion of anger.

questions.question: "The State shall take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State." This is mentioned under _________ of Constitution of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part IV**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The statement "The State shall take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State" is mentioned under Article 50 of the Constitution of India.
 
• Article 50 is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) which are enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution.
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines to the central and state governments of India, to be kept in mind while framing laws and policies.
 
• The purpose of Article 50 is to ensure the independence of the judiciary from the executive branch of the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part V**

 
 
• Part V of the Constitution of India deals with The Union.
 
• It includes provisions related to the President, Vice-President, Council of Ministers, Attorney General, Parliament, and the Union Judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Part III**
 
 
• Part III of the Constitution of India deals with Fundamental Rights.
 
• It includes Articles 12 to 35 which guarantee civil liberties such that all Indians can lead their lives in peace and harmony as citizens of India.
 
 
 
• **Part IV A**
 
 
• Part IV A of the Constitution of India deals with Fundamental Duties.
 
• It includes Article 51A which outlines the fundamental duties of every citizen of India.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**
 
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines or principles given to the central and state governments of India, to be kept in mind while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are not enforceable by any court, but the principles laid down therein are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.

questions.question: What is the literacy rate among males in India according to the Literacy Rate 2011 census?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.8214**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the 2011 Census, the literacy rate among males in India is **82.14%**.
 
• The literacy rate is defined as the percentage of literate people aged seven years and above.
 
• The 2011 Census showed a significant improvement in male literacy rates compared to previous censuses.
 
• This high literacy rate among males indicates a positive trend in educational attainment in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy Rate**

 
 
• The literacy rate is a crucial indicator of a country's educational status and development.
 
• It is calculated as the percentage of people aged 7 and above who can read and write with understanding.
 
• Higher literacy rates are often associated with better economic development and quality of life.
 
• In India, literacy campaigns and educational policies have been implemented to improve literacy rates across the country.
 
 
 
• **Census**
 
 
• A census is a systematic enumeration of a population, typically recording various details of individuals.
 
• In India, the Census is conducted every ten years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• The Census collects data on various demographic, social, and economic parameters, which are crucial for policy-making and planning.
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of India and provides comprehensive data on the population, including literacy rates.

questions.question: The term 'Dhamma' is the Prakrit word that is associated with which of the following rulers of ancient India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ashoka was one of the most important Indian emperors of the Maurya Dynasty who ruled almost all of the Indian subcontinent from c. 268 to 232 BCE.
 
• The term 'Dhamma' is associated with the teachings and edicts of Ashoka, which were inscribed on rocks and pillars throughout his empire.
 
• Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War and promoted the spread of Buddhism and the practice of Dhamma (a set of ethical and moral principles).
 
• The Dhamma of Ashoka emphasized non-violence, tolerance of all sects and opinions, and respect for all religious teachers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta II**

 
 
• Also known as Vikramaditya, he was one of the most powerful emperors of the Gupta Empire in India.
 
• His reign is marked by cultural and scientific advancements and prosperity.
 
• Chandragupta II expanded the Gupta Empire through conquest and marriage alliances.
 
• He is known for promoting the arts and literature, leading to a Golden Age of Indian culture.
 
 
 
• **Rudradaman**
 
 
• Rudradaman was a ruler of the Western Satraps in India, ruling from around 130 to 150 CE.
 
• He is known for his military conquests and administrative reforms.
 
• Rudradaman issued the Junagadh rock inscription, which is one of the longest inscriptions in classical Sanskrit.
 
• His reign was noted for the promotion of trade and culture.
 
 
 
• **Raja Raja Chola I**
 
 
• Raja Raja Chola I was a prominent king of the Chola dynasty who ruled from 985 to 1014 CE.
 
• He is best known for his extensive conquests and the expansion of the Chola Empire.
 
• Raja Raja Chola I built the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur, which is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
 
• His reign marked a period of great cultural and architectural advancements.
 
 
 
• **Dhamma**
 
 
• The term 'Dhamma' is a Prakrit word used by Ashoka to describe his policies and moral teachings.
 
• It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Dharma', which means duty, righteousness, or moral law.
 
• Ashoka's Dhamma was a set of ethical guidelines that promoted non-violence, tolerance, and compassion.
 
• The concept of Dhamma was central to Ashoka's efforts to govern his empire and promote social harmony.

questions.question: 77th Independence Day was celebrated in which of the year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2023**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's Independence Day is celebrated on **15th August** each year.
 
• The first Independence Day was celebrated on **15th August 1947**.
 
• The 77th Independence Day was celebrated in the year **2023**.
 
• Independence Day marks the end of British rule and the establishment of a free and independent Indian nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Independence Day:**

 
 
• It is a national holiday in India commemorating the nation's independence from the United Kingdom on 15 August 1947.
 
• The Independence movement was led by the Indian National Congress and many freedom fighters including Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Subhas Chandra Bose.
 
• On this day, the Prime Minister of India hoists the national flag at the Red Fort in Delhi and delivers an address to the nation.
 
• Independence Day is observed with flag-hoisting ceremonies, parades, cultural events, and the singing of patriotic songs across the country.
 
 
 
• **British Rule in India:**
 
 
• The British East India Company began its rule in India in 1757 after the Battle of Plassey and continued until 1858 when the British Crown took over following the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
 
• The period of British rule is known as the British Raj, which lasted until India gained independence in 1947.
 
• During British rule, India faced significant political, social, and economic changes, including the introduction of Western education, legal systems, and infrastructure development.
 
• The struggle for independence involved various movements and revolts against British policies and exploitation.
 
 
 
• **Freedom Fighters:**
 
 
• Several key figures played pivotal roles in India's struggle for independence, including Mahatma Gandhi, who advocated for non-violent resistance through his principles of Satyagraha and Ahimsa.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru, a prominent leader of the Indian National Congress, became the first Prime Minister of independent India.
 
• Subhas Chandra Bose led the Indian National Army (INA) against British forces during World War II.
 
• Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, and other revolutionaries contributed to the freedom struggle through armed resistance and sacrifices.

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution are primarily aimed at achieving:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Social and economic justice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government, aimed at achieving social and economic justice in India.
 
• These principles are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The objective of these principles is to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life, ensuring equitable distribution of wealth and resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**

 
 
• These principles were borrowed from the Irish Constitution and aim to establish a welfare state in India.
 
• They cover various aspects such as economic and social rights, Gandhian principles, and policies aimed at establishing international peace and security.
 
• The principles include provisions for securing a living wage, humane conditions of work, social security, and the right to education.
 
• They also advocate for the promotion of the interests of weaker sections of society, including Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs).
 
 
 
• **Economic Inequality**
 
 
• Economic inequality refers to the extent of the wealth gap between rich and poor in a society.
 
• This concept is not a focus of the Directive Principles, which aim instead at reducing inequalities through social and economic justice.
 
 
 
• **Religious Harmony**
 
 
• Religious harmony refers to peaceful coexistence and mutual respect among various religions in a society.
 
• While important, this is not the primary aim of the Directive Principles.
 
 
 
• **Political Stability**
 
 
• Political stability refers to the consistency and predictability of political institutions and governance.
 
• Although essential for development, this is not the primary aim of the Directive Principles.

questions.question: The social reformer Raja Ram Mohan Roy is associated with which socio-religious reform movement in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmo Samaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828.
 
• It aimed at reforming the prevalent Brahminical practices and emphasized monotheism, rejecting idol worship.
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is often regarded as the "Father of the Indian Renaissance" due to his efforts in social and religious reforms.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj played a crucial role in the abolition of practices such as Sati and advocated for widow remarriage and women's education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swaminarayan Movement**

 
 
• Founded by Swaminarayan (Sahajanand Swami) in the early 19th century.
 
• Focused on the worship of Swaminarayan and emphasized moral living, devotion, and community service.
 
 
 
• **Theosophical Society**
 
 
• Founded in 1875 in New York by Helena Petrovna Blavatsky, Henry Steel Olcott, and William Quan Judge.
 
• Promoted the exploration of spiritual and occult knowledge and aimed at universal brotherhood without distinction of race, creed, sex, caste, or color.
 
 
 
• **Arya Samaj**
 
 
• Founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875.
 
• Advocated for the return to the teachings of the Vedas and emphasized monotheism, equality, and social reform.
 
 
 
• **Brahmo Samaj**
 
 
• Aimed at monotheism and rejected idol worship, rituals, and the caste system.
 
• Focused on rationalism, human dignity, and social reform including the abolition of Sati and child marriage, and promotion of widow remarriage and women's education.

questions.question: Which artists have won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for contribution to Chhau dance of Seraikella?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tapan Kumar Pattanayak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tapan Kumar Pattanayak** is a renowned artist known for his significant contributions to **Chhau dance of Seraikella**.
 
• He has been recognized by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi** for his dedication and excellence in this traditional dance form.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is one of the most prestigious awards in the field of performing arts in India.
 
• Tapan Kumar Pattanayak’s work has played a crucial role in preserving and promoting the cultural heritage of Chhau dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**

 
 
• It is the highest Indian recognition given to practicing artists.
 
• The award is presented annually by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India’s National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama.
 
• It was established in 1952 and recognizes outstanding achievement in the field of performing arts.
 
• The award includes a citation, a plaque, and a cash prize.
 
 
 
• **Chhau Dance**
 
 
• Chhau is a traditional Indian dance form that combines martial, tribal, and folk traditions.
 
• It is performed in three styles named after the location where they are practiced: Seraikella (Jharkhand), Purulia (West Bengal), and Mayurbhanj (Odisha).
 
• The dance is noted for its vigorous movements and elaborate costumes.
 
• Chhau dance is traditionally performed during regional festivals, particularly the spring festival of Chaitra Parva.
 
 
 
• **Seraikella Chhau**
 
 
• It is one of the three styles of Chhau dance, originating from Seraikella in Jharkhand.
 
• This style is characterized by its use of masks, which are intricately designed and play a significant role in the dance.
 
• Movements in Seraikella Chhau are highly stylized and often depict themes from Hindu mythology.
 
• The dance form has been recognized by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

questions.question:
Read the following about Green Revolution.

A. The Green Revolution was an endeavour initiated by Norman Borlaug in the 1960s.

B. He is known as the 'Father of Green Revolution' in the world.

Identify the CORRECT statement / statements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution was indeed initiated by Norman Borlaug in the 1960s.
 
• Norman Borlaug is renowned as the 'Father of Green Revolution' globally.
 
• The Green Revolution involved a series of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives to increase agricultural production worldwide.
 
• It primarily focused on the introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, and advanced irrigation methods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Norman Borlaug**

 
 
• Norman Borlaug was an American agronomist and humanitarian who led initiatives worldwide that contributed to the extensive increases in agricultural production termed the Green Revolution.
 
• He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 for his contributions to world peace through increasing food supply.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution**
 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to a set of research and technology transfer initiatives occurring between the 1940s and the late 1960s that increased agriculture production worldwide, particularly in the developing world.
 
• It included the development of high-yielding varieties (HYVs) of cereals, especially wheat and rice.
 
• It also involved the use of synthetic fertilizers and pesticides, and the introduction of modern agricultural techniques and equipment.
 
• While it significantly boosted food production and reduced hunger in many parts of the world, it also led to environmental and social challenges, such as soil degradation, increased inequality, and dependency on chemical inputs.
 
 
 
• **High-Yielding Variety (HYV) Seeds**
 
 
• HYV seeds are seeds of better quality than normal quality seeds.
 
• They are resistant to diseases and provide a high yield.
 
• These seeds were one of the main components of the Green Revolution.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Green Revolution**
 
 
• The Green Revolution led to a significant increase in food grain production, particularly in developing countries, thus helping to avoid famines and feed growing populations.
 
• It transformed agricultural practices, making farming more intensive and reliant on chemical inputs.
 
• However, it also caused environmental damage, such as soil degradation, water scarcity, and pollution due to the overuse of fertilizers and pesticides.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the chairman of MasterCard India from September 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajnish Kumar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rajnish Kumar has been appointed as the chairman of MasterCard India from September 2023.
 
• He is the former chairman of State Bank of India (SBI).
 
• Rajnish Kumar has extensive experience in banking and financial services.
 
• His appointment is expected to strengthen MasterCard's presence and operations in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MasterCard**

 
 
• MasterCard is a global payments and technology company headquartered in Purchase, New York, USA.
 
• It is known for its comprehensive range of payment solutions including credit, debit, and prepaid cards.
 
• MasterCard operates in more than 210 countries and territories.
 
• It focuses on making transactions safe, simple, smart, and accessible.
 
 
 
• **State Bank of India (SBI)**
 
 
• SBI is the largest public sector bank in India.
 
• It provides a wide range of banking and financial services to individuals, businesses, and government entities.
 
• SBI has a significant international presence with branches in numerous countries.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the Indian banking sector and economy.
 
 
 
• **Rajnish Kumar**
 
 
• Rajnish Kumar served as the chairman of SBI from October 2017 to October 2020.
 
• He has been associated with SBI for over three decades, holding various key positions.
 
• Under his leadership, SBI took significant steps towards digital transformation and financial inclusion.
 
• Rajnish Kumar is known for his strategic thinking and leadership skills in the banking industry.

questions.question: The Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi launched 'Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat)' platform for youth of the country on October 31st 2023, at Kartavya Path on the National ________ Day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'National Unity Day' is celebrated on October 31st every year in India to mark the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who played a crucial role in the integration of India.
 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, popularly known as the 'Iron Man of India', was a key figure in India's struggle for independence and later in the unification of the country.
 
• The 'Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat)' platform aims to provide a unified platform for the youth of India to engage in nation-building activities.
 
• The launch of the 'Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat)' platform by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on this significant day underscores the importance of youth in fostering national unity and development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**

 
 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was an Indian statesman and a senior leader of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He played a leading role in the country's struggle for independence and guided its integration into a united, independent nation.
 
• He was the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of independent India.
 
• He is often referred to as the 'Bismarck of India' for his role in the political integration of India.
 
 
 
• **National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas)**
 
 
• National Unity Day, also known as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, is celebrated on October 31st every year.
 
• The day was introduced by the Government of India in 2014 to honor Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary.
 
• The day is marked by various events and activities, including the 'Run for Unity' marathon.
 
• The objective of observing National Unity Day is to reinforce the significance of unity and integrity among the citizens of India.
 
 
 
• **Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat)**
 
 
• 'Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat)' is a platform launched by the Government of India to engage the youth in various developmental activities.
 
• The platform aims to provide opportunities for the youth to contribute to nation-building and social development.
 
• It focuses on fostering leadership, community service, and skill development among the youth.
 
• The initiative is part of the government's broader vision to harness the potential of the youth for the country's progress.

questions.question: The Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 conducted by the government of India ranked households in how many categories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 was conducted by the government of India to provide comprehensive data on various socio-economic indicators.
 
• The SECC 2011 categorized households into three main categories based on their socio-economic status.
 
• The three categories were: 1) Deprived households, 2) Automatically included households, and 3) Automatically excluded households.
 
• The categorization helped the government identify and target households for various welfare schemes and programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC):**

 
 
• The SECC is a comprehensive survey conducted to collect data on various socio-economic parameters and caste information.
 
• It aims to identify households living below the poverty line and categorize them based on their socio-economic status.
 
• The data from SECC is used to implement and monitor various social welfare schemes and programs.
 
• It provides insights into the living conditions, educational status, employment, and other socio-economic aspects of households.
 
 
 
• **Deprived Households:**
 
 
• These households are identified based on specific deprivation criteria such as lack of housing, education, or employment.
 
• They are considered eligible for various government welfare schemes and programs aimed at improving their socio-economic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Automatically Included Households:**
 
 
• These households are automatically included in the welfare programs based on certain predefined criteria such as homelessness or being a bonded laborer.
 
• The criteria for automatic inclusion are designed to ensure that the most vulnerable and marginalized sections of society receive immediate assistance.
 
 
 
• **Automatically Excluded Households:**
 
 
• These households are excluded from welfare programs based on specific criteria such as owning a motorized vehicle or having a government job.
 
• The criteria for automatic exclusion are designed to ensure that resources are allocated to those who are truly in need.

questions.question: When a shuttle is hit high into the air, the player has time to hit a powerful overhand shot straight to the floor of the opponent's court. This is known as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Smash**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **smash** is a powerful overhand shot hit sharply downward into the opponent's court.
 
• It is considered one of the most offensive and aggressive shots in badminton.
 
• The smash is typically used to finish a rally and score a point.
 
• Executing a perfect smash requires precise timing, strength, and excellent positioning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Long Service:**

 
 
• In badminton, a long service is a type of serve where the shuttle is hit high and deep into the opponent's court, ideally landing near the back boundary line.
 
• It is commonly used in singles matches to push the opponent to the back of the court.
 
 
 
• **Rally:**
 
 
• A rally is a sequence of shots between opponents, starting with a serve and ending when the shuttlecock hits the ground.
 
• The objective is to keep the shuttle in play and outmaneuver the opponent to win the point.
 
 
 
• **Short Service:**
 
 
• In badminton, a short service is a serve where the shuttle is hit softly to land just over the net, typically near the front service line.
 
• It is commonly used in doubles matches to limit the opponent's attacking options.
 
 
 
• **Smash:**
 
 
• The smash is a crucial attacking shot in badminton, characterized by its speed and downward trajectory.
 
• It is often aimed at the opponent's court with the intent to end the rally and score a point.
 
• Proper technique involves a strong wrist snap and full-body coordination to maximize power.
 
• Players often jump to execute a jump smash, adding more power and angle to the shot.

questions.question:
Read the following about the Revenue expenditure.

A. Revenue Expenditure is expenditure incurred for purposes other than the creation of physical or financial assets of the central government.

B. It relates to those expenses incurred for the normal functioning of the government departments and various services, interest payments on debt incurred by the government, and grants given to state governments and other parties (even though some of the grants may be meant for creation of assets).

Identify the INCORRECT statement / statements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2 (Neither A nor B)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Revenue Expenditure** is expenditure incurred for purposes other than the creation of physical or financial assets of the central government.
 
• It relates to those expenses incurred for the normal functioning of the government departments and various services, interest payments on debt incurred by the government, and grants given to state governments and other parties (even though some of the grants may be meant for creation of assets).
 
• Statement A correctly describes Revenue Expenditure as it is not aimed at creating physical or financial assets.
 
• Statement B correctly explains the components that make up Revenue Expenditure, such as normal functioning expenses, interest payments, and grants to other entities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue Expenditure**

 
 
• Revenue Expenditure is the expenditure that the government incurs for its operational activities and routine functions.
 
• It includes salaries, pensions, interest payments, subsidies, and other routine administrative costs.
 
• This type of expenditure is not intended for the creation of assets but rather for the day-to-day functioning of the government.
 
• It is typically recurrent in nature and is accounted for within the same financial year.
 
 
 
• **Capital Expenditure**
 
 
• Unlike Revenue Expenditure, Capital Expenditure is aimed at creating physical or financial assets.
 
• It includes spending on infrastructure projects, acquisition of machinery, equipment, and other long-term investments.
 
• Capital Expenditure is typically non-recurrent and has a long-term impact on the economy.
 
• It is crucial for economic growth and development as it leads to the creation of assets that generate future economic benefits.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Deficit**
 
 
• Fiscal Deficit is the difference between the government's total revenue and total expenditure (excluding borrowings) in a given financial year.
 
• It indicates the total borrowing requirements of the government.
 
• A higher fiscal deficit implies greater borrowing and higher interest payments in the future, affecting the country's financial health.
 
• Efforts to reduce fiscal deficits include increasing revenue through taxes and reducing unnecessary expenditures.
 
 
 
• **Budgetary Allocation**
 
 
• Budgetary Allocation refers to the distribution of financial resources among various sectors and departments of the government.
 
• It is a crucial aspect of the government's budget, determining how funds will be utilized over the fiscal year.
 
• Proper budgetary allocation ensures optimal utilization of resources and effective implementation of government policies and programs.
 
• It involves prioritizing sectors such as health, education, infrastructure, defense, and social welfare based on current needs and goals.

questions.question: ________ of a substance is the temperature and pressure at which three phases (gas, liquid, and solid) of that substance may coexist in thermodynamic equilibrium.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Triple-point**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The triple point of a substance is the unique set of conditions where the three phases of matter (solid, liquid, and gas) can coexist in thermodynamic equilibrium.
 
• At the triple point, the substance can transition between the solid, liquid, and gaseous states without any change in temperature or pressure.
 
• The triple point is a fundamental concept in thermodynamics and is critical for the calibration of thermometers.
 
• Water's triple point occurs at a temperature of 0.01°C (273.16 K) and a pressure of 611.657 pascals (0.00604 atm).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Allotropic**

 
 
• Allotropy refers to the existence of an element in more than one form in the same physical state.
 
• Different forms are known as allotropes, which have different physical and chemical properties.
 
• Common examples include carbon, which exists as diamond, graphite, and graphene.
 
 
 
• **Tri-state**
 
 
• Tri-state is a term often used in electronics to describe a circuit that can exist in three different states: high, low, and high-impedance (effectively disconnected).
 
• It's not related to the phases of matter or thermodynamics.
 
 
 
• **Amphibious**
 
 
• The term amphibious refers to organisms or vehicles that can operate both on land and in water.
 
• It is not related to the concept of phases of matter or thermodynamics.

questions.question: During eighth Five year plan, India became a member of the World Trade Organization on 1 January _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1995**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India became a member of the World Trade Organization (WTO) on 1 January 1995.
 
• The World Trade Organization (WTO) is an intergovernmental organization that regulates international trade.
 
• WTO officially commenced on 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement, replacing the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT).
 
• As a member of the WTO, India has to adhere to its rules and regulations and can benefit from the international trading system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO)**

 
 
• The WTO is the only global international organization dealing with the rules of trade between nations.
 
• Its main function is to ensure that trade flows as smoothly, predictably, and freely as possible.
 
• The WTO provides a forum for negotiating agreements aimed at reducing obstacles to international trade and ensuring a level playing field for all, thus contributing to economic growth and development.
 
• The WTO also provides a legal and institutional framework for the implementation and monitoring of these agreements, as well as for settling disputes arising from their interpretation and application.
 
 
 
• **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)**
 
 
• The GATT was a legal agreement between many countries, whose overall purpose was to promote international trade by reducing or eliminating trade barriers such as tariffs or quotas.
 
• It was signed by 23 nations in Geneva on October 30, 1947, and took effect on January 1, 1948.
 
• The GATT was intended to boost economic recovery after World War II through reconstructing and liberalizing global trade.
 
• The GATT continued to exist until it was replaced by the WTO on January 1, 1995.
 
 
 
• **Marrakesh Agreement**
 
 
• The Marrakesh Agreement established the World Trade Organization, signed in Marrakesh, Morocco, on April 15, 1994.
 
• The agreement marked the culmination of the Uruguay Round of GATT negotiations, which lasted from 1986 to 1994.
 
• It resulted in the most significant reform of the global trading system since the GATT was created in 1948.
 
• The Marrakesh Agreement incorporated the GATT framework and expanded it to include new areas such as services and intellectual property.

questions.question: Pool swimming at the Olympic Games takes place inside a ________ meter-long swimming pool divided into eight lanes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**50 meters**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The standard length of an Olympic swimming pool is **50 meters**, which is used for all competitive swimming events in the Olympics.
 
• An Olympic pool is divided into eight lanes, each lane typically being 2.5 meters wide.
 
• The pool must be at least 2 meters deep, ensuring the safety and optimal performance of the swimmers.
 
• This 50-meter pool allows for long course swimming, which is a standard for international competitions like the Olympics and World Championships.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Long Course and Short Course**

 
 
• A long course pool is 50 meters in length. This is the standard for Olympic Games and World Championships.
 
• A short course pool is 25 meters in length, often used in local and regional competitions, as well as some international meets.
 
• The times recorded in long course pools are generally slower than those in short course pools due to fewer turns.
 
 
 
• **Swimming Lanes**
 
 
• Each lane in an Olympic pool is 2.5 meters wide, providing enough space for swimmers to perform without interference.
 
• Lane ropes are used to reduce turbulence and keep swimmers in their respective lanes.
 
• The lanes are numbered from 0 to 8, with lane 4 often reserved for the fastest qualifier in finals.
 
 
 
• **Pool Depth**
 
 
• The minimum depth of an Olympic pool is 2 meters, but many pools are deeper to provide better wave dissipation and swimmer safety.
 
• Deeper pools help reduce the drag effect on swimmers, enabling faster swim times.
 
 
 
• **Competition Standards**
 
 
• The Federation Internationale de Natation (FINA) is the international governing body for swimming and sets the standards for pool dimensions and equipment.
 
• FINA regulations ensure that all competitive pools meet specific criteria to provide fair and consistent conditions for all swimmers.
